critical.issue: 403 STILL not logged. $exceptions->stopIgnoring([AuthorizationException::class, UnauthorizedException::class]) is INSUFFICIENT because Spatie's UnauthorizedException extends Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpException, and Laravel's ExceptionHandler::shouldntReport() checks 'instanceof' against every class in internalDontReport (which contains HttpException). Since the exception IS-A HttpException, it is still ignored regardless of the stopIgnoring list — unless HttpException itself is also passed to stopIgnoring, OR recording is moved to $exceptions->render(function($e,$req){ ActivityLog::record(...); return null; }). Direct proof reproduced: 'app(ExceptionHandler)->report(new AuthorizationException)' → 1 row created; 'app(ExceptionHandler)->report(new UnauthorizedException(403,""))' → 0 rows created. Confirms the class-hierarchy issue.

rca_of_the_issue: Symptom: hitting /appearance as a Staf-role user returns 403 correctly, but no ActivityLog row with status_code=403 exists (verified: Setting::query 'App\Models\ActivityLog::where(status_code,403)->count()' returns 0 after the 403 hit). Root cause: In Laravel 11 the framework's Illuminate\Foundation\Exceptions\Handler::shouldntReport(Throwable $e) resolves the ignore list as array_merge($this->dontReport, $this->internalDontReport) and returns true if $e instanceof ANY class in that merged list. $internalDontReport contains Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpException. Spatie\Permission\Exceptions\UnauthorizedException EXTENDS Symfony HttpException, so instanceof returns true and the exception is still 'shouldntReport'. $exceptions->stopIgnoring([AuthorizationException, UnauthorizedException]) only removes those exact classes; it does NOT remove HttpException. Therefore the report() callback that writes to activity_log NEVER fires for a real 403 request. Verified via tinker: calling app(ExceptionHandler)->report(new AuthorizationException('t')) inserts 1 row; the SAME call on new UnauthorizedException(403,'t') inserts 0 rows. Fix (developer): (a) add HttpException::class to stopIgnoring(), OR (b) migrate recording to $exceptions->render(function(Throwable $e, $request) { if(...) ActivityLog::record(...); return null; }) which is invoked regardless of reporting rules. Also observed harmless-but-noisy Blade view errors in laravel.log ('Undefined array key meta_title') triggered by TestIteration12EmptyPersists tests exercising the empty-meta_title state — pre-existing behavior of app.blade.php reading @meta_title unconditionally; report only, not blocking.
